script: I've given up on life and I wish for it to end every single day. I am a 38-year-old female. I am stuck in a depression‑anxiety‑obesity loop that started when my doc slid me an SSRI a decade ago. That pill? It added 100 pounds to my frame and kicked off hypothyroidism. Now I am over 300lbs, and losing weight feels like trying to pull teeth out of a rock. I used to work delivering packages. I literally ran my ass off for 10‑12 hours straight, 6‑7 days a week. I lost 30lbs in that year—like, real progress, but the job was a toxic nightmare. I left, exhausted and bruised, because the environment was worse than the weight. Now I drive for a living. The moment I switched, the 30lbs came back like a bad ex, and then some. The weight's not just a number; it's a mask I wear because being seen with my husband feels like a death sentence. I am terrified his coworkers will see me and "make fun of him" or something. Nightmares haunt me. I dream my husband's running off with a hotter, thinner person. I've even tried to "run him off myself." I am calling myself a whale, a pig, a cow—like a self‑destructive mantra. He says he's tired of me tearing myself down. Back pain is my new best friend. I begged my doctor for help, anything, but I can't afford GLP‑1. I am drained, exhausted, and every breath feels like a battle. Anxiety is at an all‑time high, and my depression? It's a full‑blown tsunami. I've given up on life. I know people will judge when they see me. Society hates fat folks. So I hide in my house, praying for death. I haven't taken the plunge yet because I have kids, and I refuse to drag them through that trauma. But the longing to quit is getting stronger, stronger. I go to therapy. I am just so tired of being fat and disgusting. I am better at handling this than those people who're just living in the moment. I've survived a decade of meds that only made me heavier. I've survived a toxic job that wanted me dead. I am still standing, even if I am hiding. And that, bestie, is my story.
